description: Asynchronous messaging (Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS-style). Producers get an acknowledgement after publishing; consumers process messages in the background and call the outgoing links. Absorbs spikes as backlog (lag) instead of rejecting requests, and behaves like the technology you pick.
modeled: Publish acknowledgement latency (plus replication wait and batching linger) and a bounded backlog
Partitioned logs: key-hashed ordered partitions, one consumer each (hot partitions lag)
Fetch cycles: a consumer polls its partitions' backlog, processes it in parallel slots (each partition in order), pays the fetch and commit overhead, then polls again
Redelivery of failed messages up to max deliveries, then dead-lettering
Visibility timeouts / ack deadlines: slow processing is delivered again (duplicates)
Memory alarm flow control: publishers block past the high watermark
At-most-once delivery: overflow dropped silently; FIFO publish rate limits
Backlog (lag), consumer utilization and message age
notModeled: Broker disk and network throughput limits

presets.description: Partitioned log: messages hash by key to 12 ordered partitions, one consumer each; acks=all and 5 ms linger on publish.
presets.name: Kafka

presets.description: Message broker with competing consumers on a queue; past the memory high watermark it blocks publishers.
presets.name: RabbitMQ

presets.description: Managed HTTP queue: slower publishes, unbounded backlog, 30 s visibility timeout (slow processing gets delivered twice).
presets.name: SQS-style queue

presets.name: Pub/Sub-style topic

kafka.detail: Messages with the same key land on the same partition and are processed in order by the one consumer that owns it. A skewed key makes one partition, and its consumer, fall behind while others idle.
kafka.title: Ordered partitions, one consumer each

kafka.detail: The producer's acknowledgement waits until the in-sync replicas have the message (the default since Kafka 3.0).
kafka.title: acks=all

kafka.detail: The producer holds a message up to linger.ms to batch it with others (5 ms by default in Kafka 4.0).
kafka.title: Batching (linger.ms)

nats.detail: Core NATS is at-most-once: a slow consumer's overflow is dropped and the publisher never knows. Choose at-least-once for JetStream.
nats.title: Core NATS drops, JetStream persists

pubsub.detail: A message not acknowledged within the ack deadline is delivered again.
pubsub.title: Ack deadline (10 s)

rabbitmq.detail: When queued messages use more memory than the high watermark, the broker blocks publishing connections until consumers catch up: producers slow down instead of getting errors. Needs memory and message size set.
rabbitmq.title: Memory alarm blocks publishers

sqs.detail: A received message is hidden for the visibility timeout. If processing takes longer, the message becomes visible again and another consumer processes it too: duplicate work.
sqs.title: Visibility timeout (30 s)

sqs.detail: FIFO queues accept about 300 publishes per second without batching; standard queues are effectively unlimited.
sqs.title: FIFO throughput limit
